question: What must a saved document retain, validate and migrate, and which durable-state or migration layers can be eliminated?
trigger: The owner asked for a best-api-review audit of every open ledger unit, frozen from status at fe0e9599a6 on 2026-10-04 (39 units), and judged afresh because earlier verdicts came from a weaker model. It asked for verdicts only, so no plan, build or panel follows in this run. This scope was open as pursue-not-adopted at queue position 15. It is not the unit next returned, which was reads.
requirements: Save and reopen a complete document (children, named roots, meta) without losing supported feature state or unknown JSON metadata.
The app owns lineage and historical fingerprints; wrong lineage, unknown fingerprints, future versions, missing steps and invalid output fail before any replacement is published.
Raw historical input needs explicit source intent.
Editors admit current-schema input only; runtime, demo and CLI share one detached converter.
Migration steps see immutable target facts, never a mutable editor or plugin store.
Feature value codecs, local history and app lineage keep separate version clocks.
Unreleased targets are amended rather than versioned; the persistence owner allocates released boundaries.
evidenceReuse: This review reused the five 2026-09-16 persistence records and the decision page's hazard probes and production proof as historical evidence. At HEAD and in the live tree it rechecked documentMigrations.ts (HEAD and the uncommitted live version), run-migration.ts, assertNoPrepareDocument and its resolvePlugin call sites, migratePlateV54Inputs, value-codec and the EditorValuePersistence type, the migration demo, the plate.md persistence doctrine, the autocomplete topic Open work, and the model-document admission records and plan. documentMigrations.ts, documentMigrations.spec.ts, document-shape.ts, the CLI sources, .changeset/persistence-detached-conversion.md, the 2026-10-03/04 model records, the model plan and docs/plans/topics/autocomplete.md are uncommitted work by other sessions.
summary: The job is to save a complete document and reopen or upgrade it at the storage boundary without losing roots, metadata or feature state, with app-owned lineage and fail-closed identity. At HEAD, defineDocumentMigrations and migrateDocument form one detached converter. The converter snapshots caller input, requires explicit source intent for raw input, and preflights the chain before callbacks. Steps get immutable target facts and a typed mapSelection, and success returns a complete current envelope. Editor migrations, plugin prepareDocument and migrateElementIds are cut, and the CLI and demo call the same converter. The strongest alternatives (plain app functions, merging lineage into value-codec versions, moving the runner into Plite, one universal session store) still lose for the reasons the September review gave. At HEAD, completion fits the document and drops unknown top-level fields. The model scope's 2026-10-04 review closes step documents behind a typed legacy channel and refuses unlifted fields, and another session is building that now in uncommitted files. The autocomplete Open work labelled persistence/release holds a release-boundary allocation that the doctrine defers to release, app-owned Yjs and history cutovers, and missing tests for v54 input migration in named roots, whose code already walks roots.

alternatives: Keeping the adopted detached converter is the selected lane. It removed editor authority, input aliasing, implicit source guessing and incomplete output, and no stronger lane beats it.

Opening a persistence Pursue for unknown top-level stored fields loses. The model scope's 2026-10-04 Pursue specifies closed step documents, the legacy channel and completion refusal, and its plan is building them, so a second owner would duplicate the work.
Deleting the generic runner and leaving plain app functions loses, because fingerprint and lineage checks, chain preflight, typed selection mapping and runtime/CLI parity are repeated jobs.

Moving the whole runner into Plite loses for now. Plate owns target compilation, element-ID admission and the authored capability, and the neutral record reader and closure are already moving into Plite under the model plan.

Merging app lineage into feature value-codec versions or persisting one universal editor session loses, because codecs, local history, collaboration and app lineage have different clocks and lifetimes.
proofLimits: This is a source review only, and this audit ran no test, CLI, browser or benchmark. The live migration files carry another session's uncommitted model-admission edits, so this review cites HEAD lines where the decisive fact predates them. The claim that HEAD completion drops unknown top-level fields rests on the model review's probes and the fitDocument call, not a fresh run. If the model plan stops before adoption, the unknown-field gap returns to this scope. This review examined no saved documents outside the repository, storage provider, Yjs room or offline history. The v54 input migration in named roots and with meaningful children has code but no test.
